verdict.reasoning: Patient states hearing has been deteriorating for about six weeks and limited to the left ear: "For about six weeks" and later confirms "Just the left ear" and that symptoms are "kind of on and off."

Patient reports left ear ringing and that certain sounds trigger it: "I occasionally get like a ringing in my left ear" and "if I'm watching TV or listening to music or something. Something that will set off the ringing in the ear."

Patient describes mild dizziness with slight sickness and explicitly denies vertigo-type spinning: "a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy" and later "It's not that kind of dizziness you get with nausea, like not proper room spinning or anything like that, but just a little bit kind of off balance."

Doctor asks about pain, discharge, fever, and itchiness and patient does not report them; specifically: about fever, patient says "Not specifically, apart from the dizziness and sickness I mentioned before" and to itchiness answers "No." The absence of affirmative responses to pain and discharge questions implies denial.
Patient reports a previous brief hearing issue about a year ago: "I had something maybe about a year ago, but it only lasted a couple of days. It wasn't anything as long as this."
When asked about cotton buds, patient denies use: "Now, do you use cotton wool buds... ?" and patient replies, "No. I don't know."

No physical examination findings are documented in the transcript; instead the doctor plans a future in-person exam: "we need to get someone to have a look inside your ear" and "book you in for a face to face appointment... one of the GP will just have a quick look down the ear."

The assessment logically combines stated symptoms and differential: left-sided hearing difficulty, tinnitus, and mild dizziness are repeatedly described, and the doctor mentions possible causes such as wax obstruction or inner ear/balance system issues: "difficulty hearing in your left ear"; "ringing... called tinnitus"; "might be wax"; and "might be that there's a problem inside the drum or the balance system within the ear."

Doctor plans a face-to-face GP clinic visit within 4–5 days for otoscopic assessment and to rule out wax or other pathology: "book you in for a face to face appointment in one of our clinics... within the next four, five days or so" and "have a quick look down the ear, figure out whether there's a physical blockage or whether there's something else going on."

Doctor explicitly plans to paste a tinnitus leaflet link in the appointment notes: "I'm going to put paste the link for a leaflet about tinnitus in the notes for this appointment. I'd really appreciate it if you could start reading about it."

Doctor advises to seek help if issues arise before the clinic visit: "If there's any problem, any issues between now and when the clinic appointment is, just book another appointment and you can speak to her and we'll serve a video."
